title: Sordland/Turn02/Personal_Funeral
description: Funeral of Bernard Circas in Deyr. Petr there to support you briefly. Karl there to secure the perimeter.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Dark clouds were looming over Deyr...."
entries.dialogueText: Dark clouds were looming over Deyr. They looked daunting as our convoy started approaching the century-old cemetery.

entries.speaker: Petr Vectern
entries.title: Petr Vectern: "“Anton.”"
entries.dialogueText: “Anton.”

entries.speaker: Serge Wolkner
entries.title: Serge Wolkner: "“Sir, we have arrived.”"
entries.dialogueText: “Sir, we have arrived.”

entries.speaker: Karl Greiser
entries.title: Karl Greiser: "“Mr. President.”"
entries.dialogueText: “Mr. President.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "It looked like it was going to rain..."
entries.dialogueText: It looked like it was going to rain. Certainly fitting weather for a funeral.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "As expected, Bernard Circas's passi..."
entries.dialogueText: As expected, Bernard Circas's passing maintained its media traction and all of Sordland was paying attention to the ceremony. Especially to what I would say in my speech today.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Rain drops were running down the ca..."
entries.dialogueText: Rain drops were running down the car window when Serge opened my door and held an umbrella over my head. As soon as I got out, flashes from the cameras blinded me.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“It's okay Serge. I will hold my ow..."
entries.dialogueText: “It's okay Serge. I will hold my own umbrella.”
entries.menuText: “It's okay Serge. I will hold my own umbrella.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Thank you.”"
entries.dialogueText: “Thank you.”
entries.menuText: “Thank you.”

entries.speaker: Serge Wolkner
entries.title: Serge Wolkner: "“As you wish sir.”"
entries.dialogueText: “As you wish sir.”

entries.speaker: Serge Wolkner
entries.title: Serge Wolkner: "“It's my duty, sir.”"
entries.dialogueText: “It's my duty, sir.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "He handed me the umbrella and start..."
entries.dialogueText: He handed me the umbrella and started waiting next to the car with his own.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "He silently started following me wh..."
entries.dialogueText: He silently started following me while holding the umbrella.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Petr and Karl exited from their own..."
entries.dialogueText: Petr and Karl exited from their own cars in the convoy. They made their way over to me.

entries.speaker: Karl Greiser
entries.title: Karl Greiser: "“I just wanted to inform you that t..."
entries.dialogueText: “I just wanted to inform you that the perimeter is clear and secured completely. There is no one getting in or out without our knowledge.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“We don't want something similar ha..."
entries.dialogueText: “We don't want something similar happening again, do we?”
entries.menuText: “We don't want something similar happening again, do we?”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“You better be right for your sake...."
entries.dialogueText: “You better be right for your sake.”
entries.menuText: “You better be right for your sake.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Good work. Thank you Karl.”"
entries.dialogueText: “Good work. Thank you Karl.”
entries.menuText: “Good work. Thank you Karl.”

entries.speaker: Karl Greiser
entries.title: Karl Greiser: "“I have taken the necessary precaut..."
entries.dialogueText: “I have taken the necessary precautions. I personally made sure of that. We are all safe.”

entries.speaker: Karl Greiser
entries.title: Karl Greiser: "“Absolutely not, Mr. President. The..."
entries.dialogueText: “Absolutely not, Mr. President. The same mistakes will never happen again. I personally made sure of that.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Karl bowed his head with respect."
entries.dialogueText: Karl bowed his head with respect.

entries.speaker: Petr Vectern
entries.title: Petr Vectern: "“Good. If anything happens to Anton..."
entries.dialogueText: “Good. If anything happens to Anton, you will have to answer to the First Lady.”

entries.speaker: Petr Vectern
entries.title: Petr Vectern: "“And trust me Karl. You don't want..."
entries.dialogueText: “And trust me Karl. You don't want that.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Petr let out a laugh, which drew so..."
entries.dialogueText: Petr let out a laugh, which drew some attention from bereaved attendees.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Petr, you are being inconsiderate...."
entries.dialogueText: “Petr, you are being inconsiderate.”
entries.menuText: “Petr, you are being inconsiderate.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“I don't think any of us want that...."
entries.dialogueText: “I don't think any of us want that.”
entries.menuText: “I don't think any of us want that.”

entries.speaker: Player_Italic
entries.title: Player_Italic: "I gestured at Petr to lower his voi..."
entries.dialogueText: I gestured at Petr to lower his voice a bit.
entries.menuText: Gesture Petr to lower his voice.

entries.speaker: Petr Vectern
entries.title: Petr Vectern: "“You are right. Sorry.”"
entries.dialogueText: “You are right. Sorry.”

entries.speaker: Petr Vectern
entries.title: Petr Vectern: "“You are right. Sorry.”"
entries.dialogueText: “You are right. Sorry.”

entries.speaker: Petr Vectern
entries.title: Petr Vectern: "“Indeed.”"
entries.dialogueText: “Indeed.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "It started to rain. Several unintel..."
entries.dialogueText: It started to rain. Several unintelligible voices were heard from Karl's radio. He stepped out to reply and returned shortly.

entries.speaker: Karl Greiser
entries.title: Karl Greiser: "“We have a small problem, sir.”"
entries.dialogueText: “We have a small problem, sir.”

entries.speaker: Karl Greiser
entries.title: Karl Greiser: "“A few -- five to be exact -- Red Y..."
entries.dialogueText: “A few -- five to be exact -- Red Youth members are here to attend the funeral. They apparently said they wish to pay their respects to their fallen comrade.”

entries.speaker: Karl Greiser
entries.title: Karl Greiser: "“Should we let them in?”"
entries.dialogueText: “Should we let them in?”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Let them in.”"
entries.dialogueText: “Let them in.”
entries.menuText: “Let them in.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Absolutely not, it is too risky.”"
entries.dialogueText: “Absolutely not, it is too risky.”
entries.menuText: “Absolutely not.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Do you think they pose a security..."
entries.dialogueText: “Do you think they pose a security threat?”
entries.menuText: “Do you think they pose a security threat?”

entries.speaker: Karl Greiser
entries.title: Karl Greiser: "“No. They were thoroughly searched...."
entries.dialogueText: “No. They were thoroughly searched. It looks like they really are here to attend the funeral.”

entries.speaker: Karl Greiser
entries.title: Karl Greiser: "“As you command.”"
entries.dialogueText: “As you command.”

entries.speaker: Petr Vectern
Petr Vectern
entries.title: Petr Vectern: "“Let's head over. They are about to..."
entries.dialogueText: “Let's head over. They are about to start.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "We walked towards the crowd circled..."
entries.dialogueText: We walked towards the crowd circled around the grave. Everyone in attendance was wearing black in mourning. The rain started pouring heavily.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Let them in but put a few guards o..."
entries.dialogueText: “Let them in but put a few guards on them to be safe.”
entries.menuText: “Let them in but put a few guards on them.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Bernard's widow and daughter were i..."
entries.dialogueText: Bernard's widow and daughter were in the front row, staring at the coffin with a mixture of disbelief, confusion and above all, a cold, unforgiving sadness.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Before taking my place to observe t..."
entries.dialogueText: Before taking my place to observe the ceremony, I gave my condolences to Bernard's wife and his daughter who looked at me. She reminded me of Deana.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Both of their eyes were very red an..."
entries.dialogueText: Both of their eyes were very red and swollen from weeping.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "When the religious ceremony was don..."
entries.dialogueText: When the religious ceremony was done, I was invited by the priest to deliver my speech. I took the podium. I felt like I had a lump in my throat. I couldn't get the daughter's eyes out of my head.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Today, we are mourning Bernard Cir..."
entries.dialogueText: “Today, we are mourning Bernard Circas, a father, a husband and a loyal servant of this country.”
entries.menuText: “Today, we are mourning Bernard Circas, a father, a husband and a loyal servant of this country.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Towards the back of the crowd, I sp..."
entries.dialogueText: Towards the back of the crowd, I spotted the members of the Red Youth, wearing red shirts and black bands of mourning on their arms. They seemed ruly and were respectfully bowing their heads.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "There was complete silence except f..."
entries.dialogueText: There was complete silence except for the sound of raindrops.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Regardless of his ideology, this w..."
entries.dialogueText: “Regardless of his ideology, this was a heinous act made towards a good man. We must end this cycle of violence now.”
entries.menuText: “Regardless of his ideology, this was a heinous act made towards a good man. We must end this cycle of violence.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“I interpret this attack as an atta..."
entries.dialogueText: “I interpret this attack as an attack against Sordland and by extension, against me personally.”
entries.menuText: “I interpret this attack as an attack against Sordland and by extension, against me personally.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“We will make sure that unfortunate..."
entries.dialogueText: “We will make sure that unfortunate events such as this will never happen ever again.”
entries.menuText: “We will make sure that unfortunate events such as this will never happen again.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“He was a true comrade and he fough..."
entries.dialogueText: “He was a true comrade and he fought for what he believed in, his ideal vision of Sordland, in every step of his life. We must learn from him.”
entries.menuText: “He was a true comrade and he fought for what he believed in, his ideal vision of Sordland, in every step of his life.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“A moment of silence please.”"
entries.dialogueText: “A moment of silence please.”
entries.menuText: “A moment of silence please.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Thank you.”"
entries.dialogueText: “Thank you.”
entries.menuText: “Thank you.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“I would now like to recite a part..."
entries.dialogueText: “I would now like to recite a part from one of the poems he left us.”
entries.menuText: “I would now like to recite one of the poems he left us.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Our only strength is the will to s..."
entries.dialogueText: “Our only strength is the will to survive, knowing that we will perish, knowing nothing more absolute.”
entries.menuText: “Our only strength is the will to survive, knowing that we will perish, knowing nothing more absolute.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“I promise you this. The blood of B..."
entries.dialogueText: “I promise you this. The blood of Bernard will not remain on the sacred ground of Sordland.”
entries.menuText: “I promise you this. The blood of Bernard will not remain on the sacred ground of Sordland.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "During the silence, all that was he..."
entries.dialogueText: During the silence, all that was heard were the ravens.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Some attendees started clapping, so..."
entries.dialogueText: Some attendees started clapping, some crying.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "The coffin was lowered into the gra..."
entries.dialogueText: The coffin was lowered into the grave by the gravekeepers. After a couple of minutes, Bernard Circas was with the soil, no more.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "The widow thanked me with a soft an..."
entries.dialogueText: The widow thanked me with a soft and defeated voice before we dispersed.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "On my way back to the car, I still..."
entries.dialogueText: On my way back to the car, I still couldn't get the eyes of Bernard's daughter, nor the faltering voice of his wife, out of my head. Would Deana, Monica and Franc look the same way if something happened to me?

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Petr put his hand on my shoulder."
entries.dialogueText: Petr put his hand on my shoulder.

entries.speaker: Petr Vectern
entries.title: Petr Vectern: "“That was a good speech.”"
entries.dialogueText: “That was a good speech.”

entries.speaker: Petr Vectern
entries.title: Petr Vectern: "“Come on, it's time to go.”"
entries.dialogueText: “Come on, it's time to go.”

entries.speaker: Petr Vectern
entries.title: Petr Vectern: "“We've got work to do.”"
entries.dialogueText: “We've got work to do.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "I sensed only respect in his voice."
entries.dialogueText: I sensed only respect in his voice.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "He was right. We had work to do. So..."
entries.dialogueText: He was right. We had work to do. So much more to do.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Thank you. I mean it.”"
entries.dialogueText: “Thank you. I mean it.”
entries.menuText: “Thank you. I mean it.”

entries.speaker: Petr Vectern
entries.title: Petr Vectern: "“I know you do.”"
entries.dialogueText: “I know you do.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "I realized that the rain had stoppe..."
entries.dialogueText: I realized that the rain had stopped, and I looked up.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "The black clouds slowly dispersed a..."
entries.dialogueText: The black clouds slowly dispersed and sunbeams enlightened our surroundings.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“This is a great loss for all of us..."
entries.dialogueText: “This is a great loss for all of us, for our country.”
entries.menuText: “This is a great loss for all of us.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“As we bid farewell to Bernard, I w..."
entries.dialogueText: “As we bid farewell to Bernard, I want to close with the words every Sord lives by: A Morgna wes core!”
entries.menuText: “As we bid farewell to Bernard, I want to close with the words every Sord lives by: A Morgna wes core!”

entries.speaker: Player_Italic
entries.title: Player_Italic: "I stepped down from the podium. It..."
entries.dialogueText: I stepped down from the podium. It was time to leave.
entries.menuText: Step down from the podium.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Everyone replied: “Vectern sis da!”..."
entries.dialogueText: Everyone replied: “Vectern sis da!”. Victory is close.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "With applauses, I stepped down from..."
entries.dialogueText: With applauses, I stepped down from the podium. It was time to leave.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "As someone once said: 'Even the dar..."
entries.dialogueText: As someone once said: 'Even the darkest night will end and the sun will rise.'

entries.speaker: Player_Italic
entries.title: Player_Italic: "I nodded."
entries.dialogueText: I nodded.
entries.menuText: Nod.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“The tears of the family he left be..."
entries.dialogueText: “The tears of the family he left behind have a price that needs to be paid. I will not stop until it is paid in full.”
entries.menuText: “The tears of the family he left behind have a price that needs to be paid. I will not stop until it is paid in full.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Let us all mourn the passing of Be..."
entries.dialogueText: “Let us all mourn the passing of Bernard Circas and remember him well.”
entries.menuText: “Let us all mourn the passing of Bernard Circas and remember him well.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“But, hatred begets hatred. There i..."
entries.dialogueText: “But, hatred begets hatred. There is only one way to overcome this vicious cycle. We must unite against the evil of this world.”
entries.menuText: “But, hatred begets hatred. There is only one way to overcome this vicious cycle. We must unite against the evil of this world.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“It's time to go.”"
entries.dialogueText: “It's time to go.”
entries.menuText: “It's time to go.”

entries.speaker: Petr Vectern
entries.title: Petr Vectern: "“Agreed.”"
entries.dialogueText: “Agreed.”

entries.speaker: Petr Vectern
entries.title: Petr Vectern: "“Hah! Right? I mean, life is full o..."
entries.dialogueText: “Hah! Right? I mean, life is full of tragedy. We should try to take it easy if we can.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“You are the only one that can make..."
entries.dialogueText: “You are the only one that can make me laugh at a funeral.”
entries.menuText: “You are the only one who can make me laugh at a funeral.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“I will confess that I disagreed wi..."
entries.dialogueText: “I will confess that I disagreed with Bernard Circas almost entirely. But it doesn't mean that he deserved this. Our country can be a better place.”
entries.menuText: “I will confess that I disagreed with Bernard Circas almost entirely. But it doesn't mean that he deserved this. Our country can be a better place.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Circas had a dream of a unified So..."
entries.dialogueText: “Circas had a dream of a unified Sordland. In these next months we need to fulfill his dream and band together.”
entries.menuText: “Circas had a dream of a unified Sordland. In these next months we need to fulfill his dream and band together.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Hope was still on the horizon."
entries.dialogueText: Hope was still on the horizon.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“We rise, toward the sun! Those who..."
entries.dialogueText: “We rise, toward the sun! Those who died, died fighting. They are now buried in the sun. No need to mourn, there is a raid to the sun."
entries.menuText: “We rise, toward the sun! Those who died, died fighting. They are now buried in the sun. No need to mourn, there is a raid to the sun."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""They did not let us sing our songs..."
entries.dialogueText: "They did not let us sing our songs. They are afraid, afraid of the dawn. They are afraid of hope, but our songs will be sung."
entries.menuText: "They did not let us sing our songs. They are afraid, afraid of the dawn. They are afraid of hope, but our songs will be sung."

entries.speaker: Petr Vectern
